title: Can the shoe sizes be arranged in another way?
description: A question from the book asks whether the shoe-size data can be arranged in any other way. The video removes the repeats of the ordered row and builds a second arrangement, checking that no student is lost.
teaching_notes: One idea: write each value once and put its count beside it. Watch for children who write the sizes once but forget the counts.

source: Figure it Out: are there other ways to arrange the data
video_script.why: The child builds a second arrangement of the same data and checks it against the first.
video_script.substitution: none: the book's own shoe-size data
video_script.anchor: Jia's ordered row of shoe sizes
video_script.payoff_line: Yes, the data can be arranged in a frequency table.

final_answer.value: Yes, the data can be arranged in a frequency table.
final_answer.spoken: yes, the data can be arranged in a frequency table

names.Jia: teacher who recorded the shoe sizes of her students

never_show: the words frequency table before the answer
video_script.design: The ordered row of 27 sizes on the left; on the right, a two-column table that fills up step by step.

beats.on_screen: title card with the long ordered row of shoe sizes from 3 to 7 and an empty box beside it

marks.scene: the title card arrives with the ordered row
marks.only: the empty box beside the row lights up
marks.ask: a question mark lights up in the box

narration: <bookmark mark='scene'/>This is a question from your book about the shoe sizes of Jia.
<bookmark mark='only'/>Her ordered row is one way to show the data.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>Is there another way to arrange it?

beats.on_screen: the ordered row and the question mark stay on the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

beats.on_screen: the ordered row with every block of equal sizes lit, and the length of each block marked

marks.repeat: each block of equal sizes lights up
marks.long: the length of the longest block is marked

narration: <bookmark mark='repeat'/>The ordered row repeats a size once for each student who wears it.
<bookmark mark='long'/>That makes the row long, even though there are only five different sizes.

beats.on_screen: Given: the ordered row of 27 shoe sizes: five different sizes, 3 to 7

marks.given: the ordered row is written as the given

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, the ordered row of twenty seven sizes, from three to seven.

beats.on_screen: To find: another way to arrange the same data

marks.find: the line to find is written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find another way to arrange the same data.

beats.on_screen: Step 1: write each different size once: 3, 4, 5, 6, 7

marks.sizes: the five different sizes are written once each in a column

narration: <bookmark mark='sizes'/>Step one, write each different size once in a column.
These are three, four, five, six and seven.

beats.on_screen: Step 2: beside each size, the number of students: 3 has 3, 4 has 9, 5 has 10, 6 has 4, 7 has 1

marks.counts: the length of each block is counted and written beside its size

narration: <bookmark mark='counts'/>Step two, count each block and write its number beside the size.
The numbers are three, nine, ten, four and one.

marks.check: the five numbers are added in a line under the table

narration: <bookmark mark='check'/>Step three, add the numbers to check the table.
They make twenty seven, so no student is lost.

beats.on_screen: Answer: Yes, a frequency table: each size once, with its number of students
narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>Yes, the data can be arranged in a frequency table.
